name: Ecuador
snapshot: Daniel Noboa's war on gangs has brought joint operations with the US and a fourth curfew this year, while the arrest of his twice-defeated rival Luisa González has critics warning of one-party rule.
culture: Ecuador spans Pacific beaches, Andean highlands, the Amazon and the Galápagos Islands, where Darwin observed finches. Quito's colonial centre was among the first UNESCO World Heritage sites. Kichwa communities keep strong Andean traditions, and the Panama hat is actually made in Ecuador, woven from toquilla straw.
society: Ecuador uses the US dollar and is the world's largest banana exporter. In a few years, drug gangs turned it from one of the region's safest countries into one of its most violent, with prisons run by cartels. Noboa declared an "internal armed conflict" in 2024. Indigenous movements have led powerful protests against fuel price rises.
situation: Ten years ago Ecuador was one of South America's safer countries, wedged between the world's two biggest cocaine producers, Colombia and Peru, but largely spared their violence. Then its ports became the main exit for cocaine to Europe and the US, and the gangs followed. By 2025 it had the highest murder rate in Latin America, about 52 per 100,000, roughly one killing an hour (AFP via FMT). Daniel Noboa, a banana-fortune heir elected at 35, has answered with soldiers, prisons and a close alliance with Trump. In November 2025 voters rejected his plan to allow foreign military bases, a sharp personal rebuke.

In 2026 Noboa took the war across his border and into trade. In January he blamed Colombia's leftist president Gustavo Petro for failing to fight cocaine and illegal gold mining along the frontier, and slapped a 30 percent "security tariff" on Colombian goods; he raised it to 50 percent in March and 100 percent from 1 May (Al Jazeera). Petro called it a "monstrosity" that meant the end of the Andean trade pact for Colombia, and cut off cross-border electricity sales that Ecuador depends on during droughts. On 3 March Noboa and Trump launched a joint military operation in Ecuador against what the US calls designated terrorist organisations; Petro alleged bombs fell near farms on the border (Al Jazeera). The government says killings are finally falling: 14 percent fewer in the first quarter, 28 percent fewer in March, though 1,800 people had still been murdered by early April (El Diario). Critics say the war targets the poor while money launderers go untouched.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for four years with one re-election and can dissolve the unicameral National Assembly once, triggering new elections for both. Ecuador uses the US dollar as its currency.
holders: President Daniel Noboa (ADN), since November 2023, re-elected April 2025.

update.html: On 22 October police arrested Luisa González, the Citizen Revolution candidate who came second to Noboa in 2023 and 2025, in a money laundering investigation into alleged undeclared funding for her 2023 campaign, and a judge ordered her held before trial. Her party, led by exiled former president Rafael Correa, calls it political persecution; Correa says Ecuador is living under a dictatorship. An electoral court had already barred her from the 29 November local elections. On 1 November Noboa imposed the year's fourth night curfew, in five provinces. On 10 November the National Assembly granted Noboa 14 days' leave to campaign in the local elections, in two blocks from 12 to 18 and 20 to 26 November, and Vice President María José Pinto is acting president while he is away.

story: Quito was part of the Inca Empire before the Spanish conquest. Independent in 1830, Ecuador swung between coastal Guayaquil's business elite and the highland capital. Oil was found in the Amazon in 1967. It adopted the US dollar in 2000 after a banking collapse. Since 2020, drug gangs moving cocaine through its ports have made it one of Latin America's most violent countries.
